questions.explanation: 'Because' introduces a cause — the event was postponed due to bad weather.

questions.text: Ms. Tanaka ___ with the client for over three years.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous 'has been working' describes an action that started in the past and continues to the present, indicated by 'for over three years'.

questions.text: The new printer is ___ than the old one.
questions.explanation: The comparative form 'more efficient' is needed because two things are being compared, indicated by 'than'.

questions.text: There has been a ___ increase in sales this quarter.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'significant' modifies the noun 'increase'.

questions.text: All documents must ___ by the department head before publication.
questions.explanation: Passive voice 'be approved' is needed — documents are approved by someone, not doing the approving.

questions.text: We look forward to ___ you at the annual conference.
questions.explanation: After the phrase 'look forward to', a gerund (-ing form) is required: 'meeting'.

questions.text: The conference room is ___ for up to fifty people.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'available' describes the conference room's capacity.

questions.text: Mr. Lee is responsible ___ managing the IT department.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition after 'responsible' is 'for'.

questions.text: Employees ___ wash their hands before returning to work.
questions.explanation: 'Should' expresses a recommendation or obligation, appropriate for a hygiene requirement.

questions.text: The committee will ___ a decision by next Wednesday.
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is 'make a decision', not 'do' or 'take' a decision.

questions.text: The candidate ___ resume impressed the hiring manager was offered the position.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession — the resume belongs to the candidate.

questions.text: The report was ___ by the senior analyst.
questions.explanation: The past participle 'written' is used in the passive voice construction 'was written'.

questions.text: The store is ___ offering a 20% discount on all electronics.
questions.explanation: The adverb 'currently' modifies the verb 'is offering', meaning 'at the present time'.

questions.text: If we had more time, we ___ the project thoroughly.
questions.explanation: In a second conditional (present unreal), 'would + base verb' is used: 'would complete'.

questions.text: The first item on the ___ is the budget review.
questions.explanation: 'Agenda' refers to a list of items to be discussed at a meeting.

questions.text: The number of applicants for the position ___ increased significantly.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb, so 'has' is correct.

questions.text: The training session will take place ___ Tuesday morning.

questions.text: ___ the high cost, the company decided to proceed with the project.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' is followed by a noun phrase ('the high cost'), not a full clause.

questions.text: The client decided to ___ our offer due to pricing concerns.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'turn down' means to reject or refuse an offer.

questions.text: The new policy ___ take effect starting January 1st.
questions.explanation: Future tense 'will' is used for a future event: 'will take effect'.

questions.explanation: The noun 'requirement' is needed as the complement: 'a requirement for this position'.

passages.title: Part 7: Reading Comprehension — Single Passage 3
passages.instructions: Read the passage and answer the questions.
passages.text:
The rise of remote work has fundamentally transformed the way businesses operate. Before 2020, only a small percentage of employees worked from home regularly. Today, hybrid work models — where employees split their time between the office and home — have become the norm at many companies.

Proponents of remote work argue that it increases productivity, reduces overhead costs, and improves employee satisfaction. Studies have shown that remote workers often report higher levels of focus and fewer interruptions compared to their office-based counterparts. Additionally, companies can save significantly on real estate, utilities, and office supplies.

However, remote work is not without its critics. Some managers struggle with monitoring performance and maintaining team cohesion. There are also concerns about employee burnout, as the boundary between work and personal life becomes blurred. Younger employees, in particular, may miss out on mentorship opportunities that naturally occur in an office setting.

To address these challenges, many organizations have adopted hybrid models. A common approach is to require employees to be in the office two or three days a week for collaboration, while allowing remote work on other days. This model attempts to balance the benefits of flexibility with the advantages of in-person interaction.

Looking forward, experts predict that the trend toward flexible work arrangements will continue. Companies that embrace this shift are likely to have a competitive edge in attracting and retaining talent. Those that resist may find themselves at a disadvantage in an increasingly globalized and digital economy.

This expansion is expected to reduce our overall energy costs by an additional 15%, bringing our total energy savings to approximately 55%. We are also exploring battery storage solutions to address the intermittency of renewable sources.

While the upfront costs have been significant — $2.3 million to date — we project that the investment will pay for itself within four years. We remain committed to reducing our carbon footprint while maintaining profitability.

Sincerely,
David Henderson

The concept of corporate social responsibility (CSR) has evolved significantly over the past few decades. Once viewed as merely a public relations exercise, CSR is now a core business strategy for many organizations. Companies are increasingly expected to demonstrate their commitment to environmental sustainability, ethical labor practices, and community engagement.

One of the most visible aspects of modern CSR is environmental sustainability. Many corporations have set ambitious targets for reducing carbon emissions, minimizing waste, and transitioning to renewable energy. Some have gone further by redesigning their supply chains to reduce environmental impact at every stage, from raw material sourcing to product disposal.

Ethical labor practices represent another critical dimension. Consumers and investors alike scrutinize how companies treat their workers, both directly employed and those in their supply chains. Issues such as fair wages, safe working conditions, and the elimination of child labor have become central to corporate reputation. Companies that fail to address these issues risk not only reputational damage but also legal consequences, as governments tighten regulations around supply chain transparency.

Community engagement, the third pillar of CSR, takes many forms. Some companies donate a percentage of profits to local charities, while others encourage employees to volunteer during work hours. Still others invest in educational programs or infrastructure in the communities where they operate. The most effective CSR programs are those that align with a company's core competencies — for example, a technology company funding coding classes in underserved schools.

Critics argue that some CSR initiatives are little more than 'greenwashing' — superficial efforts designed to improve public image without meaningful change. However, research suggests that genuine CSR programs can enhance brand loyalty, attract top talent, and even improve financial performance. As stakeholder expectations continue to rise, CSR is likely to become even more integral to business success.

The convenience factor is significant — what once required a two-hour round trip can now be accomplished with a few clicks.

However, challenges persist. Delivery times remain longer in rural areas, and shipping costs can be higher. Some rural post offices have struggled with the increased volume of packages. Artificial intelligence is reshaping the financial services industry in ways that were unimaginable just a decade ago. From automated trading algorithms to chatbots that handle customer inquiries, AI technologies are being deployed across every segment of the financial sector.

One of the most significant applications of AI in finance is in fraud detection. Traditional fraud detection systems relied on rule-based algorithms that flagged suspicious transactions based on predefined criteria. AI-powered systems, by contrast, can analyze vast amounts of data in real time, identify patterns that human analysts might miss, and adapt to new types of fraud as they emerge. Major banks report that AI has reduced false positives — legitimate transactions incorrectly flagged as fraudulent — by up to 50%, saving both money and customer goodwill.

Another area where AI is making inroads is in credit scoring. Conventional credit scoring models use a limited set of data points, such as payment history and debt-to-income ratios. AI models can incorporate a much wider range of variables, including utility payments, rental history, and even social media behavior. Proponents argue this leads to more accurate assessments, particularly for individuals with limited credit history. Critics, however, raise concerns about privacy and the potential for algorithmic bias.

Robo-advisors represent yet another AI application. These automated platforms provide investment advice and portfolio management at a fraction of the cost of traditional financial advisors. While they have democratized access to investment management, some financial experts caution that robo-advisors may not perform well during periods of market volatility, when human judgment and experience are most valuable.

Despite these advances, the integration of AI in finance faces regulatory hurdles. Governments and regulatory bodies are still grappling with how to oversee AI-driven financial services. Questions about accountability, transparency, and consumer protection remain unresolved. As AI continues to evolve, the financial industry will need to balance innovation with responsibility.

--- PASSAGE 1: ARTICLE ---

THE SHIFT TOWARD SUSTAINABLE PACKAGING

By Laura Bennett, Environmental Correspondent

Consumer goods companies are facing increasing pressure to adopt sustainable packaging solutions. With growing awareness of plastic pollution and its environmental impact, both regulators and consumers are demanding change.

Several major brands have already made significant commitments. Unilever has pledged to make all packaging recyclable, reusable, or compostable by 2025. Procter & Gamble has introduced refillable product lines, and Nestlé has invested heavily in biodegradable materials. These initiatives reflect a broader industry trend toward circular packaging — systems where materials are reused rather than discarded.

The transition, however, is not without challenges. Sustainable packaging materials are often more expensive than conventional plastics. Biodegradable alternatives may require specific composting conditions that are not widely available. Additionally, some eco-friendly materials have shorter shelf lives or may not provide the same level of product protection.

Despite these obstacles, the market for sustainable packaging is growing rapidly. According to industry analysts, the global market is expected to reach $412 billion by 2027, up from $289 billion in 2022. Government regulations, particularly in Europe, are accelerating this growth by mandating reductions in single-use plastics.

Consumers play a crucial role in this transition. Studies show that 73% of consumers are willing to pay more for products with sustainable packaging. However, there remains a gap between intention and action — many consumers say they prefer eco-friendly options but do not consistently choose them at the point of purchase.

--- PASSAGE 2: MEMO ---

MEMORANDUM
To: Product Development Team
From: VP of Sustainability
Date: June 18
Subject: New Packaging Initiative

Following the industry trends outlined in the attached article, our company is launching a comprehensive packaging redesign initiative. The goal is to transition 80% of our product line to sustainable packaging within three years.

Phase 1 (Year 1): Audit current packaging materials and identify the top 10 products for priority redesign. Budget: $500,000.

Phase 2 (Year 2): Develop and test new packaging prototypes. Conduct consumer testing to ensure product quality is maintained. Budget: $750,000.

Phase 3 (Year 3): Roll out new packaging across all priority products and begin transition of remaining products. Budget: $1,200,000.

Key requirements for new packaging:
- Must be recyclable or compostable
- Must maintain product shelf life
- Must not increase retail price by more than 5%
- Must be sourced from suppliers with verified sustainability certifications

The Product Development Team will lead this initiative, with support from Marketing and Supply Chain departments. A project kickoff meeting is scheduled for July 1 at 10:00 AM in the main conference room.

Product: AeroClean Air Purifier (Model AC-700)
Date of Purchase: July 15
Customer: Robert Chen

Overall Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3/5)

Performance: The air purifier works well in small rooms (up to 200 sq ft). It effectively reduces dust and allergens. However, it struggles in larger spaces. I placed it in my living room (450 sq ft) and noticed minimal improvement.

Noise Level: On the lowest setting, it is very quiet. On the highest setting, it is quite loud — too loud to watch TV comfortably. A medium setting works well for daily use.

Filter Replacement: The filter needs replacing every 6 months. Replacement filters cost $45 each, which seems expensive for a product in this price range. The indicator light that signals filter replacement is helpful.

Design: The design is sleek and modern. It fits well in most decors. The touch controls are responsive.

Value for Money: At $199, it is reasonably priced for a small-room purifier but overpriced for larger spaces. I would recommend it for bedrooms or small offices.
